items.question: How long does a Tape-In system last?
items.answer: With proper care, natural tape-in hair can last a year or longer, and several years if handled gently. The system can be reused many times.

items.question: Can I correct the tapes myself?
items.answer: Yes. You can re-tape at home without visiting a stylist every time. When you buy hair, we send recorded video lessons on working with tapes, and you can learn the technique in depth in our training.

items.question: What's the difference between Imitation 2.0 and 1.0?
items.answer: Imitation 1.0 leaves a small visible edge of about 2–3 mm and takes 5–7 days to make. Imitation 2.0 is fully hand-stitched, hair by hair, so there is no visible edge; it takes 3–4 weeks to make.

items.question: How do I choose a colour?
items.answer: The most accurate way is to visit us in Tbilisi and hold a strand against your hair at a consultation. You can also use the colour palette on the site as a guide.

items.question: How much does a system cost?
items.answer: For example, 50 cm, 100 g of hair on Imitation 1.0 costs $390, and on Imitation 2.0 it costs $520. We calculate the exact price on request: it depends on length, weight, shade and technique.

selfCorrection.title: Self-correction
selfCorrection.description: Once you've learned the technique in a course, the tapes can be repositioned yourself at home. You don't have to visit a stylist every time — you just need the right materials and to follow the method strictly.
selfCorrection.warningText: Below is a general sequence of correction steps, not a complete protocol. The step-by-step method is covered in the video lessons we send when you buy hair and in our training course. Correction without preparation, or with the technique not followed, can damage your own hair.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.description: Gather the materials for removing and reinstalling the tape, and wash and dry your hair without oils or conditioners near the roots.

steps.title: Removing the old tape
steps.description: Carefully dissolve the adhesive with a tape remover, without pulling or forcefully combing the strands.

steps.title: Preparing the strand
steps.description: Section off a strand the same width as the tape, and clean any adhesive residue from the roots.

steps.title: Installing the new tape
steps.description: Firmly and evenly attach the tape at the root, following the technique learned in training.

steps.title: Check
steps.description: Make sure the tape sits evenly and doesn't pinch your natural hair, adjusting if needed.

selfCorrection.disclaimer: Doing it yourself takes care and following the technique. If you have no experience, study the instructions first and see a professional if needed.

academyBridge.text: Correction is a separate block of the Da Vinchi training programme: an online video course or in-person classes in Tbilisi.

care.title: Care & lifespan
care.description: How to wash, style and look after your extensions so they keep their length and thickness longer.
rules: Shampoo goes on the scalp and the attachment area.
Masks, conditioners, oils and leave-in products go on the lengths, away from the tapes.
Heat protection and moderate temperatures keep your hair in good condition.
A correction every 2–2.5 months on average keeps the extensions comfortable and neat.
Gentle care helps keep length and thickness for a long time.
Extend at home or with a stylist: choose the format that suits you.
closing: We select natural hair around your wishes so the extensions look harmonious and home care stays as familiar as possible.
Our goal is not just to add length and thickness, but to help you enjoy beautiful hair and create the looks you love again and again.
Natural hair. Individual selection. Beauty that stays with you.

selfCorrectionBridge.text: Repositioning tapes the wrong way shortens the system’s lifespan. It is safer to learn the technique first.
